data.name: ROOT
data.detailed_description:
Step into the inexpensive loafers of expert hacker Edward Summerton. Roll up your sleeves, pop your collar and brew a pot of coffee, because today you're going to breach the networks of a mysterious and powerful corporation.

ROOT is a cyber espionage themed hardcore stealth FPS that lets you play it how you want: whether creeping along corridors undetected or bursting into rooms to blow away all adversaries. Cyber terrorism is a dangerous profession, and risks have real consequences. Damage sustained cannot be recovered, the slightest mistake will jeopardize your chances to reach the next level.

During this undertaking of corporate crypto-espionage you will face many hostile programs, but your most dangerous enemy is the man who designed them. The Systems Administrator built the System from the ground up and holds immense power within the network. He will use the limitless resources at his disposal to prevent you from achieving your goal: total ROOT access to the System.

FEATURES

/// Accurate Guns ///

Your crosshair is literally a dot. No reticule bloom, no accuracy cones, no B.S. Your shot lands where the cursor points.

/// Real Stealth ///

No "crouch for invisibility," you must tread softly and check your corners.

/// Boss Fights ///

Be prepared for tough, end of level fights. Only truly dangerous enemies are satisfying to defeat.

/// Interactive Environment ///

Objects can be moved, shot, shattered, picked up and thrown.

///Abstract Visuals ///

The inside of a computer is not what you expect.

/// Old School Mentality ///

This is a game, not a movie. You are in control of all your actions. No QTEs or long animated cut scenes.

/// Vaguely Witty Dialogue [On/Off] ///

Listen to your companion, SHELL, ramble on about various things, which may or may not pertain to the story arc. Don't care what he has to say? Just turn off dialogue in the options menu.

reviews.review:
I found this game, just ok. I didn't really have much fun in the end, but I also didn't completely hate what I went through. It was kind of dull, but still had some cool moments and I did want to get to the end.

ROOT is basically a stealth focused FPS with very tight maze like levels.You can also try to play aggressive if you want but prepare for enemies to rush you down. If you play stealth, the main way to get through the game is sneaking up on enemies and smacking them on the back of there neck. You do have guns which can help in more isolated areas, but will attract enemies from other rooms potentially. There's basically a pistol and a shotgun, and they are also kind of weak, but I think that's ok since the stealth is the focus here. You can also kick enemies, throw objects as distractions, and holler to attract enemies.

For a stealth game, the enemy AI and level design are pretty lacking. All enemies have pretty straight forward walking paths. When you distract them or get caught they immediately go to the location, spin around a bit to check their surroundings, and then teleport back to their patrol path. If they detect you they stand in place and attack you (or they keep chasing you for some enemies) and if you run far enough, they lose you and teleport back. The lack of gadgets or interesting environmental interactions really makes these interactions kind of uninteresting. Distracting enemies also feels kind of pointless because of the teleporting aspect which makes it hard to take advantage of it. So most of my gameplay was waiting to see enemy paths, and whack them in the back if I see the opening for it. Sometimes I also just rushed past using the dodge move to get to the elevator or a vent and tanked damage since that could be faster then slowly sneaking or waiting for an opening. I will say that there is some cool enemy variety such as the robots that don't see you if you stay still, a scary headless ghost enemy that's really hard to run from and a mimic enemy. There's also 2 unique bosses (first one is repeated another time), which are not stealth based at all and feel like dark souls bosses, but they were honestly kind of lame with you having to let them try to attack so you dodge them and then shoot them during this opening and repeat.

The level design is really lacking here. you basically have rooms with enemies patrolling separated by doors you can use to peak. Sometimes there are vents you can freely move through and that's kind of it. Your goal is basically, get to the elevator and sometimes you need to get enough clearance levels or keys to get to the end. Sometimes these feel randomly placed so you're just kind of trying to run around the level randomly until you know where all the things are. Because of this I would mostly play carelessly at first just to get an idea of where everything I need is and what enemies would be in my path. Then I actually used stealth knowing generally where to go. You don't have much health and enemies are pretty spongy so knowing where to go makes it easier not to get caught. Due to the hacker theme, all levels look the same basically; blue office spaces with green and white things you can pick up and lots of boxes sometimes (technically you can stack these to climb up places but the levels don't have interesting designs where that really comes up overall). Some levels feel basically like trial and error runs and since this is a stealth game, some times it really sucked having to repeat certain aspects of a level where I'm just waiting. That being said the levels are pretty short so it's mostly not a big deal.

I think the lack of interactivity is what mostly hurts this game. Stealth games are fun because you can manipulate AI in all sorts of wacky ways to solve problems, but you don't really have much you can do here other then sneak by, knock out, kill or distract. The most you get is the enemy variety, but they don't really fundamentally change the gameplay much for stealth. I can see this game being kind of cool for the kind of person who likes a simple predictable game that you can try to optimize, such as finding the optimal path for beating a level, and maybe trying things like no kill runs. I did also like I can speed around using the side dash move.

So overall, it's a competent game with all the basic elements needed for a stealth fps, but lacking in fun factor.
